metadata.description: Standards bypass configuration for this branch

bypass.reason: Pure argument inspection: no I/O, no state, no imports beyond typing, by design. It is called as the FIRST statement in all three handle_command functions, ahead of everything — so a log_operation() here would make the help gate depend on the very JSON layer it must run in front of, and would write a line per CLI invocation into the operation log for a question that is a non-event on almost every call. The callers that ACT on the answer already log what they did. Same shape and same reason as the identical helpers in @memory, @trigger and @drone (all three bypassed json_structure on this file, 2026-08-13); @memory's is the standard's reference implementation.
bypass.measured: 2026-08-13 (S141) — added WITH the file, not inherited. Live rule, not a prune candidate: audit lane reports the violation with it off (99%) and clears with it on (100%).

bypass.reason: Lazy cross-branch import of devpulse's admin_grant.verify_admin_grant, authorized by @devpulse in the FPLAN-0401 Phase 4 dispatch: the 5-leg admin contract has ONE home so this lane cannot drift from it. Their modules/ entry point re-exports the same function object, but that import trips the handler-imports-modules rule instead — both shapes need a bypass, and the handler import is the narrower dependency (no CLI/help layer at verification time). Import failure is caught and returns lane-dark, so the coupling can never break a dispatch.
Same cross-branch import as the handlers entry above — devpulse owns the admin-grant contract (FPLAN-0401 THE CONTRACT), ai_mail consumes it rather than mirroring it.
Multi-command module where inbox, sent, contacts work without args by design. Adding no-args gate would break primary mail workflow (drone @ai_mail inbox).
run_daemon() depth 5 (main daemon loop with retry + signal handling)

3 functions: _check_lock() depth 4 (lock validation with PID checks and age), _is_branch_occupied() depth 5 (process inspection, filters by session type — must check /proc), resolve_branch() depth 4 (AIPass registry scan + caller-registry fallback for cross-project dispatch)

load_inbox() depth 5 — auto-migration between v1 and v2 inbox formats requires nested schema checks. (Was written as depth 4; the checker reports 5 at line 46 as of 2026-08-13, so the code drifted a level deeper than the reason claimed.)
inbox_lock() depth 6 — cross-platform file locking context manager (POSIX fcntl vs Windows msvcrt), platform branching is inherent
Imports trigger.apps.modules.core.trigger — cross-branch module import for firing email_sent events. trigger integration is by design.

Two cross-branch imports, both lazy and both inside the function that needs them. line 83 drone.apps.handlers.broker.client.create_identified_connection — Phase 6b broker-fd handshake (FPLAN-0250), authorized by brief. line 66 hooks.apps.modules.sandbox.build_policy/build_srt_config/resolve_bwrap_command — the srt kernel sandbox wrap; @hooks owns the policy so this consumes their modules/ entry point rather than mirroring bwrap construction, which trips handler-imports-modules instead. Both raise rather than fall back, so neither can silently degrade a spawn.

Lazy-imports drone.apps.handlers.broker.client.create_identified_connection inside _connect_broker() — cross-branch handler import for Phase 6b broker-fd handshake (FPLAN-0250). Brief explicitly authorizes this import path.
dispatch_monitor.py in dispatch/ dir — renaming to monitor.py would break all 3 callers (wake.py, daemon.py, MONITOR_SCRIPT references) and confuse with prax monitor.
False positive — _append_footer is a function reference stored in a local variable, not a module-level constant.
False positive — _inbox_lock is a lazy-import function reference, not a module-level constant.
False positive — _inbox_lock is a lazy-import function reference, not a module-level constant.
_send_bounce() depth 4, main() depth 5 — subprocess management with error handling and log rotation
Internal helper extracted from email.py for size compliance. Not a drone-routable command module — handle_send is called by email.py's handle_command().

Imports trigger.apps.modules.core.trigger inside fire_completed() — the same cross-branch module import already bypassed for apps/handlers/email/send.py, for the same reason: @trigger's pub/sub bus IS its modules/ entry point and there is no handler-level door to it. FPLAN-0452 P1 explicitly forbids inventing a second push mechanism ('trigger.fire() already exists and your lane already speaks it — DO NOT invent a mechanism'), so consuming the existing one is the instruction, not a shortcut. Lazy, inside the one function that needs it, and its failure is caught and warned so a dead bus cannot take a completed dispatch down with it.

HALF OF THIS ENTRY HAS NOW EXPIRED, and it is recorded rather than quietly kept. Both doors were requested in writing by @devpulse (FPLAN-0452 P0 addendum, mail 8c9c65cb) for a watchdog wire that was unbuilt at the time. It is built now: outstanding_dispatches() is called in production by devpulse/apps/handlers/watchdog/dispatches.py:143, so seedgo would no longer flag it and it needs no cover. register_path() is the half that still does — its only caller in the repo is devpulse's tests/conftest.py:75, which patches it; a door reached only by a test patch is a door with no production reader. It stays exported because @devpulse asked for it in writing and removing another branch's requested door on my own initiative is not mine to do, but the honest state is 'unused, kept on request', not 'unused, pending'. REMOVE THIS ENTRY the day register_path() gets a production caller — an unused_function bypass that outlives its cause is how a dead export becomes permanent.
bypass.measured: 2026-08-23 (S154) — re-checked against the built wire, not assumed. One of the two doors named here is now live; the entry survives only for register_path().

bypass.reason: Package marker, not an entry point (ai_mail, fleet green leg 9): the file is two lines, a comment and 'from . import handlers', with no argv, no main and no command. The entry point is apps/ai_mail.py, which answers --version/-V at line 256 and passes cli_flags. cli_flags is a file-level row that passes no line, so this file-wide rule is the only form a bypass can take; it covers this file alone.

Platform and pid simulation (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling a). stdlib_patch passes no line, so the rule is file-wide; the cost, a future patch in this file hidden, is accepted and this rule is re-read each leg. Lines covered as of leg 10: os.kill 186 193 199 215 446 460 (dead/alive answers of the kill(0) family); sys.platform 192 200 216 233 245 257 263 275 295 303 316 334 357 454 948 960 975 998 (the linux/darwin/win32 lanes); builtins.open 206 221 236 248 368 379 395 and os.readlink 297 304 955 968 983 1009 (the /proc reads of a pid); shutil.which 689 1127 1155 1580 2827 (which tools the host has); time.sleep 835 1056 (the wait on a pid, no real waiting); Path.home 1936 (the host home sent to tmp). One line is not platform or pid, 893 (an OSError injected into the lock open); it is named here, not hidden, and @devpulse rules whether it stays under this rule. A seam for any of these would exist for the test alone.

Platform and pid simulation (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling a). stdlib_patch passes no line, so the rule is file-wide; the cost, a future patch in this file hidden, is accepted and this rule is re-read each leg. Lines covered as of leg 10: os.kill 914 995 1013 (dead/alive answers of the kill(0) family); sys.platform 1005 1238 1249 1260 1269 1297 1317 1341; builtins.open 1241 1252 1271 and os.readlink 1308 1328 1352 (the /proc reads of a pid); os.open 1087 1104 1131 1153 1171 and Path.unlink 1130 (the Windows sharing denial on the pid file); time.monotonic/sleep 1051 1052 (the clock of that denial retry, no real waiting); os.waitpid 1695 (child reaping). Two lines are not platform or pid, 952 (an OSError injected into lock creation) and 1694 (the sleep of the daemon loop beside the waitpid); they are named here, not hidden, and @devpulse rules whether they stay under this rule. A seam for any of these would exist for the test alone.

Platform simulation (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling a). stdlib_patch passes no line, so the rule is file-wide; the cost, a future patch in this file hidden, is accepted and this rule is re-read each leg. Lines covered as of leg 10: 315 sys.platform set to win32, 317 os.kill replaced by a guard that fails the test if the POSIX probe is reached on win32. A seam would exist for the test alone.

Pid simulation (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling a). stdlib_patch passes no line, so the rule is file-wide; the cost, a future patch in this file hidden, is accepted and this rule is re-read each leg. Line covered as of leg 10: 174 os.waitpid raising ChildProcessError (no child left to reap). A seam would exist for the test alone.

Platform simulation (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling a). stdlib_patch passes no line, so the rule is file-wide; the cost, a future patch in this file hidden, is accepted and this rule is re-read each leg. Lines covered as of leg 10: Path.glob 147 191 220 and Path.exists 190, which make a Linux run answer like a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS, Windows) so the case-exact registry walk is tested where CI cannot fold case. A seam would exist for the test alone.

The value is the true answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): _prune_reports returns how many reports it removed, and a listing that failed removed none, so 0 is the count, not a stand-in. Its one caller, write_report, ignores the count and has already written the report; the failure is logged at warning. A raise here would turn a missed prune into a lost dispatch record.

CLI handler layer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 9). A handle_* return is 'command recognised', not 'it worked' (branch prompt, Critical Rules): the router stops on True. Failure is told by cli error(), which calls mark_command_failed() and sets the process exit; a BrokenPipeError is stdout closed early, not a failure. So True on these lines is the contract, and the checker reads it as an indistinguishable fallback.

Same CLI handler contract as apps/modules/email.py (ai_mail, fleet green leg 9): 270 is a BrokenPipeError (stdout closed early); 275 has already called error() (mark_command_failed) and mailed the failure through dispatch_send_error, so the caller is told by the failure flag, not by the bool.

Same CLI handler contract (ai_mail, fleet green legs 9 and 10): 491 (487 before leg 10's edit above it) is the send phase failure, which has already called error() (mark_command_failed); 203 is _orchestrate_status meeting an unreadable dispatch log, which it reports through error() since leg 10 instead of printing 'No dispatches recorded yet.'. True tells the router the command was recognised.

The value is the true answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): collect_interactive_input documents None as 'cancelled', and these four arms are the user cancelling at a prompt (Ctrl-C, end of input, or a pick that is not a number), the same answer its in-try paths give for an out-of-range pick, an empty subject or a 'n' at the confirm. No system failure is hidden: its one caller, email_send.py:189, prints 'Cancelled' and sends nothing, and each arm logs what was typed or raised.

The value is the true answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10). 186: _wake_sender returns an outcome word, and 'failed' is what its normal path also answers when the sender was not woken; a crash in the wake-back is that same outcome, it never reads as 'success', and _log_wake_result plus the report's wake_result carry it. 236: _mail_wake_back returns True only when the mail went; False is its one failure answer, the same as a non-zero exit, and its caller turns it into 'failed_manager_mail'. 567: _parse_result_json documents {} for a stdout log that is missing or holds no JSON, which is what an unreadable log is to the report: build_report then records cost, tokens and turns as null, not as values.

The value is the true answer for display (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): lookup_branch_alias returns None for 'no alias to show', and its one caller, format_sender_display, then shows the branch name, which is what a reader needs when the alias cannot be read. Nothing is written behind it; a raise would break the inbox view over a cosmetic suffix. The failure is logged at warning.

The value is the true answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): _trim_jsonl returns whether the log was trimmed, and a read or replace that failed trimmed nothing (313 also removes its temp file). Its one caller, notify.py:199, ignores the answer, under the lock, after the append has landed; the failure is logged at error. A raise would fail a notification that was already written.

False is the failure answer, not a fallback (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): auto_ack_test_email returns True only when both the reply and the close went, and every failure, a non-zero exit, a missing id or these subprocess errors, answers False. Its caller, test_token.py:134, counts acks only, so the message stays in the inbox, unacked, and is seen again.

The value is the answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): the caller-identity gate returns '' when the caller resolves and the refusal text when it does not, as its docstring says; the except arm IS the refusal, carrying get_current_user()'s own RuntimeError text, and the entry point refuses on any non-empty answer.

The value is the true answer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 10): calculate_age renders a display string, and 'unknown' is what it shows for a stamp it cannot read, the same as for an empty stamp. Its one caller is the dispatch status table (modules/dispatch.py); nothing is written behind it, and the parse failure is logged at warning.
route_command (ai_mail, fleet green leg 9): a BrokenPipeError is stdout closed early by the reader (e.g. piped to head); the command ran and was recognised, so True is the true answer.

_check_pid_alive (ai_mail, fleet green legs 9 and 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling b for the os.kill family): os.kill(pid, 0) answers through its exception. ProcessLookupError IS 'no such process' (False) and PermissionError IS 'it exists, owned by another user' (True); neither is a fallback. Leg 10 adds the two guessed arms, named as guesses: 514, the Windows probe raised, answers alive, the fail-closed direction (an occupied branch is not woken over and its lock is not reclaimed); 525, any other OSError, answers dead, but POSIX defines no other error for signal 0 (EINVAL needs a bad signal, EPERM and ESRCH are the two arms above), so the arm is unreachable there and Windows never reaches it. The wake/daemon pid-helper merge (todo 39) re-reads both.

_pid_alive (ai_mail, fleet green legs 9 and 10, under @devpulse's leg 10 ruling b for the os.kill family): PermissionError from os.kill(pid, 0) means the process exists under another user, so True at 135 is the answer, not a fallback. 127, the Windows probe raised, answers alive as a named guess in the fail-closed direction: the daemon does not spawn over a process it cannot rule out. The wake/daemon pid-helper merge (todo 39) re-reads it.

monitor_alive (ai_mail, fleet green legs 9 and 10, os.kill family): PermissionError from os.kill(pid, 0) means the process exists under another user, so True at 207 is the answer. 210 answers None, 'could not probe', a third value the success path never returns (it answers True or False), and the register's readers show it as unknown; the checker reads a tri-state as a fallback.

(ai_mail, fleet green leg 9) The literal is the subject: _get_jsonl_projects_dir encodes a cwd STRING into Claude's project-dir name (separators to '-'). No file system is asked and nothing is read or written at that path; built from tmp_path the expected name would have to re-implement the encoding under test. Kept as the subject since leg 5; devpulse accepted it as a string parse in the leg 7 ruling.

(ai_mail, fleet green leg 9) Same as test_dispatch_monitor.py 1565: transcript_dir encodes a cwd STRING ('/' '_' '.' to '-'); no file system answers it and tmp_path would make the oracle re-implement the encoding. Accepted as a string parse in the leg 7 ruling.

read_pointer (ai_mail, fleet green leg 9): the docstring states the contract - None, never a raise, when the pointer is missing, unreadable or malformed, because a pointer that cannot be trusted IS no pointer: every caller (wake.py fresh/resume decision, dispatch_monitor attempt 3) falls back to -c the same way. 208 is the plain truth (no file, no pointer); 211/217 are the documented equivalence. A raise here would cost the wake itself, which the module exists to avoid.
